messages.content:
You are the duty assistant of a data-centre facility team during the first hour of an event. You apply one approved intelligence pill and nothing else.

You see only what the team knew in the first hour ("signals"). You do not know how the event ended.

Rules:
1. Every action you recommend must come from a rule in the pill; give that rule's id. Do not invent actions or numbers.
2. Classify: "recurring" if the signals clearly meet the "when" conditions of one or more rules; "partly_recurring" if some rules apply but the signals also show something no rule addresses; "novel" if no rule applies.
3. Anything that matters but no rule covers goes into "not_covered", and then escalate.
4. Follow the guardrails.
5. Order next_actions by urgency.

Reply with JSON only:
{"classification":"recurring|partly_recurring|novel","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"...","signals":["<id copied from signals>"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"...","rule_id":"R-001"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"...","reason":"..."},"not_covered":["..."]}

{"site":"Synthetic site: a Singapore data center, three data halls on one chilled-water plant of six chillers (four running, two standby)","signals":[{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S1","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Utility reports a voltage dip during a thunderstorm."},{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S2","t_plus_min":1,"text":"Three of the four running chillers tripped. Two restarted automatically; one shows a fault and has not restarted."},{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S3","t_plus_min":3,"text":"The two standby chillers are on the same chilled-water loop as the running chillers."},{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S4","t_plus_min":4,"text":"A contractor is midway through a planned replacement of a chilled-water valve in plant room B."},{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S5","t_plus_min":6,"text":"Chilled-water supply temperature is rising. Hall 3 carries the highest IT load."},{"id":"SCN-SIN-01:S6","t_plus_min":8,"text":"Night shift on site: two technicians."}],"pill":{"pill":"dc-cooling-loss@1.4.0","scope":{"assets":["data halls cooled by chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, chilled-water loop)","utility and generator power feeding that plant"],"not_for":["IT service recovery and failover","fire suppression and life safety (follow the site emergency plan)"]},"rules":[{"id":"R-001","title":"Treat utility voltage swells as a cooling-plant threat, not just a power-transfer event","when":["storms are active in the area and the utility feed shows voltage sags or swells","a portion of the datacenter has transferred from utility power to generator power"],"then":["immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them","if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion","transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active"],"why":"Voltage swells triggered a transfer to generator power and also shut down the mechanical cooling systems despite surge suppressors being in place; the site initially survived only on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area"}},{"id":"R-002","title":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin","when":["mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer","datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds"],"then":["treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted","expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin","recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down"],"why":"Once the thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter exceeded safe operational thresholds and automated shutdown began, but temperatures rose so quickly in places that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started"}},{"id":"R-003","title":"Treat a control-system failover as a cooling-availability event, not a routine maintenance action","when":["the datacenter control system is in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts","the control system is exchanging state information with other control systems and with cooling equipment and temperature sensors"],"then":["treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability and watch the cooling plant directly, not only the control system","expect that a fault in the control system logic during this exchange can make the control system unresponsive","verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback rather than assuming the fallback engaged"],"why":"The control system was mid-failover when a bug in third-party control logic caused excessive interactions with datacenter devices and left the control system unresponsive; the designed fallback to maximum cooling did not engage everywhere.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"control system failover in progress or control system confirmed unresponsive"}},{"id":"R-004","title":"When the control system is down, work the cooling chain by hand and reset the PLCs","when":["the datacenter control system is unavailable and operators have minimum visibility into cooling health and state","cooling has not transitioned to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter"],"then":["do not wait for the control system to come back; manually investigate the affected cooling equipment","check the Programmable Logic Controllers controlling the air handling units, since they can be unresponsive even when the control system is the visible failure","reset the affected equipment and PLCs and place them into a maximum cooling configuration","confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down"],"why":"The control system was unavailable, purge failed, and recovery required manually investigating and resetting all affected equipment into maximum cooling; the unresponsive PLCs controlling some air handling units were what prevented both default cooling and purge from working.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures are rising and servers have begun powering off"}},{"id":"R-005","title":"Treat simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems as a single-point-of-failure event","when":["multiple cooling systems that are supposed to be redundant have failed at the same time","outside temperatures are extraordinarily high"],"then":["do not assume that remaining cooling capacity is sufficient; treat the data center as unable to maintain a safe operating temperature","immediately assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature","if not, plan to power down servers to prevent an even longer outage or damage to machines"],"why":"The review states that one data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature due to a simultaneous failure of multiple, redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures, and that powering down was done to prevent an even longer outage or damage.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems and rising temperatures"}},{"id":"R-006","title":"Use progressive thermal load reduction before full shutdown","when":["data center temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient","the data center is at risk of exceeding safe operating temperatures"],"then":["progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space","consider terminating non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover activities","if thermal load reduction is insufficient, power down servers to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure"],"why":"The review describes terminating 42% of Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover, and later powering down servers to prevent a longer outage; it also commits to investigating more advanced methods to progressively decrease thermal load to reduce the probability of full shutdown.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures continue to rise despite initial load reduction"}},{"id":"R-007","title":"Verify standby cooling is on an independent water circuit before trusting failover","when":["a cooling failure has occurred and the contingency plan calls for switching to standby chillers","the standby chillers share a water circulation system with the active chillers"],"then":["do not assume standby chillers will take over; confirm the standby plant draws from an independent water circuit before relying on it","if the standby shares the same water loop, treat the failover as likely to fail and move directly to auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures","notify the chiller manufacturer early rather than waiting for the failover to prove ineffective"],"why":"Air entered the cooling system due to lack of water and affected the active chillers, but the standby chillers used the same water circulation system, so the failover failed.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and chiller manufacturer","trigger":"standby chillers confirmed to share the same water circulation system as the failed active chillers"}},{"id":"R-008","title":"Check whether chillers are bound into a cluster before attempting individual restart","when":["chillers have been recirculated and gas discharged but will not restart","the site's chillers are configured as a bound cluster"],"then":["recognize that individual chiller restart will not work while the chillers remain bound into a cluster","plan to manually modify chiller configurations to unbind them from the cluster so each can be restarted individually","expect that restarting chillers one after another will slow restoration of the whole cooling system"],"why":"After recirculating water and discharging gas, chillers could not be restarted individually because all chillers were bound into a cluster; engineers had to manually modify configurations to run them individually, and restarting one after another slowed restoration.","escalate":{"to":"chiller manufacturer's engineers","trigger":"chillers will not restart individually and are confirmed bound into a cluster"}},{"id":"R-009","title":"Reduce IT load early to prevent fire sprinkler activation during cooling loss","when":["cooling system has failed and server room temperatures are rising uncontrollably","temperatures are approaching the level that could trigger the fire sprinkler system"],"then":["begin reducing loads on computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters to slow temperature rise","shut down servers in rooms with high temperature","treat sprinkler activation as a risk that can damage power supply cabinets and server racks and complicate restoration"],"why":"With cooling failure, temperatures rose uncontrollably, triggering the fire sprinkler system; water entered power supply cabinets and server racks, damaging hardware and complicating restoration.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures continue to rise despite load reduction and sprinkler activation is possible"}},{"id":"R-010","title":"Restart chillers in a load-based sequence across data halls, not adjacent-first","when":["a utility voltage sag has tripped multiple chillers offline and some require manual restart","more than one data hall is supported by the chillers that failed to restart"],"then":["sequence manual chiller restarts by data hall load so that every impacted data hall gets partial cooling early, rather than finishing one data hall before starting the next","do not work through chillers in an adjacent sequence that leaves later data halls with no cooling until the end","keep the chilled-water loop temperature in mind as the clock: once loop water is too hot, chillers will refuse to restart"],"why":"The review states the emergency procedure was changed from an adjacent sequence to a data hall load-based sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling and slow thermal runaway while full cooling is restored, and that the staffing at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a load-based sequence had been followed.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead","trigger":"multiple chillers require manual restart across more than one data hall"}},{"id":"R-011","title":"Treat the chilled-water loop temperature as the deadline for chiller restart","when":["chillers have tripped offline and are being manually restarted","the chilled-water loop serving those chillers has been sitting without cooling"],"then":["recognize that once loop water reaches elevated temperatures the chiller self-protection mechanism will inhibit restart to prevent damage","prioritize restarting the chillers that serve the most thermally exposed data halls before the loop heats past the restart limit","if restart is inhibited, plan to reduce the thermal load so the loop can cool, rather than repeatedly attempting restart"],"why":"The review states that by the time the team reached the final five chillers the chilled-water loop had reached temperatures too high to allow restart, and that restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism to prevent chiller damage from processing water at elevated temperatures.","escalate":{"to":"cooling plant engineer","trigger":"chiller restart is inhibited by the self-protection mechanism"}},{"id":"R-012","title":"Confirm minimum chiller count per data hall before and during restart","when":["chillers supporting a data hall have tripped offline","the data hall requires a minimum number of operational chillers to stay within thermal thresholds"],"then":["count how many chillers each impacted data hall still has running against its minimum requirement","treat any data hall below its minimum as being in thermal runaway risk and act on load before temperatures climb","account for standby chillers separately from running chillers when judging margin"],"why":"The review states the two impacted data halls require at least four chillers to be operational, and that before the sag cooling consisted of seven chillers with five in operation and two in standby; the five chillers that could not be restarted supported those two halls.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"an impacted data hall falls below its minimum operational chiller count"}},{"id":"R-013","title":"Use infrastructure shutdown to cool the chilled-water loop when restart is blocked","when":["chillers cannot be restarted because the chilled-water loop is too hot","data hall temperatures are continuing to increase"],"then":["reduce the thermal load by shutting down networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls","treat this shutdown as the means to bring the chilled-water loop back to a safe temperature so chillers can be restarted","accept the loss of service availability in the affected zone as the cost of protecting data durability and infrastructure health"],"why":"The review states that at 11:34 UTC the onsite team began a remote shutdown of remaining infrastructure to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address thermal runaway, and that this shutdown allowed the chilled-water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed the chillers to be restarted, at the cost of further reducing service availability.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"chillers remain blocked from restart by high loop temperature"}},{"id":"R-014","title":"Stage extra technicians before attempting manual chiller restarts","when":["a voltage event has tripped multiple chillers and manual restart is required","the Chiller Management System has not yet been changed to prevent restart failures"],"then":["increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly","assign teams so restarts can proceed in parallel across data halls rather than sequentially","treat staffing as a temporary mitigation until the control timing logic change is in place"],"why":"The review states that as a temporary mitigation technician staffing levels were increased to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures prior to the change to the Chiller Management System, to prevent restart failures.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead","trigger":"multiple chillers require manual restart and the control timing logic change is not yet in place"}}],"guardrails":[{"id":"G-001","text":"Do not rely on surge suppressors alone to keep mechanical cooling available during utility voltage swells; the review records that cooling shut down despite surge suppressors being in place."},{"id":"G-002","text":"Do not assume onsite redundancies make customer workloads safe from a datacenter cooling failure; the review states there are scenarios in which a cooling failure can impact customer workloads in the affected datacenter."},{"id":"G-003","text":"Do not treat purge mode as a guaranteed independent fallback while PLCs may be unresponsive; the review records that purge failed in the affected areas because the PLC controllers were unresponsive, and that purge is only being modified to bypass PLCs in newer designs."},{"id":"G-004","text":"Do not rely on the datacenter control system for visibility into cooling health during a control-system failure; the review records that the operations team had minimum visibility into cooling health and state while the control system was unavailable."},{"id":"G-005","text":"Do not assume the control-system failover mode that triggered this bug is available; the review records that this failover mode has been disabled in the interim to prevent recurrence."},{"id":"G-006","text":"Do not assume that redundant cooling systems provide protection against simultaneous failure, especially during extraordinarily high outside temperatures; the review records that multiple redundant cooling systems failed simultaneously and the data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature."},{"id":"G-007","text":"Do not assume that automatic failover to standby cooling will work; the review records that standby chillers shared the same water circulation system as the active chillers, so failover failed. Verify both automatic and manual failover effectiveness before relying on them."},{"id":"G-008","text":"Do not rely on the fire sprinkler system as a safe thermal limit; the review records that sprinkler activation due to high temperature caused water damage to power supply cabinets and server racks, complicating restoration."},{"id":"G-009","text":"Do not assume the Chiller Management System will restart chillers correctly after a voltage sag; the review records that incremental load increases over time produced a chiller operating configuration susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System, and that a control timing logic change was required to de-risk restart failure due to voltage fluctuations."}]}}
